prompt: Which row correctly identifies two forces that form a genuine Newton's third law interaction pair?
options: the upward normal contact force on a box from a floor and the downward gravitational pull of the Earth on the box
the forward thrust of an aircraft engine and the backward air resistance on the aircraft wings
the gravitational force of the Moon on the Earth and the gravitational force of the Earth on the Moon
the tension in a towrope pulling a caravan and the friction exerted by the road on the caravan tires

answer.explanation: Option 3 is correct. The gravitational force of the Moon on the Earth and the gravitational force of the Earth on the Moon act on two different bodies, are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and share the exact same physical nature (gravitational).

distractor_explanations: Option 1 describes two forces acting on the same body (the box) of different physical types (contact normal vs gravitational).
Option 2 describes two opposing horizontal forces acting on the same body (the aircraft).
Option 3 meets all four criteria for a true Newton's third law pair.
Option 4 describes two different horizontal forces acting on the same body (the caravan).
hints: Check all four criteria: equal magnitude, opposite direction, same physical type, and acting on two DIFFERENT bodies.
If both forces act on the same object, they can never be a third law pair.
solution: The gravitational force of the Moon on Earth and of Earth on the Moon form a true third law pair.
teacher_walkthrough: Evaluate Option 1: both act on the box, so they fail the different bodies criterion.
Evaluate Option 2: both act on the aircraft, failing the different bodies criterion.
Evaluate Option 3: force of Moon on Earth and force of Earth on Moon act on different bodies and are both gravitational. This satisfies all criteria.
Evaluate Option 4: both act on the caravan, failing the different bodies criterion.
